gaps.lead: The company has a good reputation in the local area.
gaps.sentence: The company ___ of in the local area.
gaps.explanation: 'People speak highly of it' becomes the passive 'it is highly spoken of'.

gaps.lead: I want you to stop tapping your pen while I am working.
gaps.sentence: I ___ tapping your pen while I am working.
gaps.explanation: 'I want you to stop' becomes 'I wish you would stop' — wish + would for irritation.

gaps.lead: Although the traffic was heavy, we reached the airport in time.
gaps.sentence: We reached the airport in time ___ traffic.
gaps.explanation: 'Although the traffic was heavy' becomes 'despite the heavy traffic' — despite + noun phrase.

gaps.lead: You didn't tell me about the meeting, and you should have.
gaps.sentence: You really ___ me about the meeting.
gaps.explanation: ought to have + participle = should have done (but didn't).

gaps.lead: The committee probably won't change the rules.
gaps.sentence: ___ the committee will change the rules.
gaps.explanation: probably won't = it is (highly) unlikely that.

gaps.lead: They cancelled the match because of the rain.
gaps.sentence: The match ___ because of the rain.
